slides.heading: Reception — Spring 2, Week 3
slides.sub: New sounds taught directly, practised and applied in words, captions and the matching decodable book.

slides.heading: Mon
slides.objective: Learn the new sound "ow" (/aʊ/) and start reading and spelling words that use it.

slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="cow" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="cow"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.mnemonic: Otis the owl flaps out and hoots a loud, surprised ow-ow when a branch wobbles under him.

character.name: Otis
character.blurb: Otis gives a startled ow-ow hoot whenever his branch wobbles unexpectedly beneath him.

slides.pronunciation_note: A loud, gliding sound, 'ow' as in 'cow' — start wide and glide down, like a little yelp of surprise.
slides.formation_cue: Write 'o', then 'w', close together — two letters, one sound.
slides.action: Throw both arms out wide as if wobbling off balance and yelp ow-ow.
slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="cow" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="cow"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.tip: The 'a' sounds like 'or' here, not its usual short sound — spread your arms out wide when you say 'all' to remember it means everything.

slides.heading: Tue
slides.objective: Learn the new sound "oi" (/ɔɪ/) and start reading and spelling words that use it.

slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="coin" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="coin"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.mnemonic: Oskar the caterpillar bumps into a shiny leaf and calls out a sharp oi-oi in surprise.

character.name: Oskar
character.blurb: Oskar bumps into things more than any other caterpillar and always calls out a sharp oi-oi.

slides.pronunciation_note: A short, sharp gliding sound, 'oi' as in 'coin' — start rounded and glide quickly to a smile, like calling out.
slides.formation_cue: Write 'o', then 'i', close together — two letters, one sound.
slides.action: Throw one hand up like calling out to a friend and say a sharp oi-oi.
slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="coin" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="coin"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.heading: Wed
slides.objective: Learn the new sound "ear" (/ɪə/) and start reading and spelling words that use it.

slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="ear" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="ear"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.mnemonic: Edie the sparrow leans in close and tilts her head, ear-ear, whenever a sound is far away.

character.name: Edie
character.blurb: Edie is a sharp-eared sparrow who tilts her head and leans in close to catch quiet, faraway sounds.

slides.pronunciation_note: A gliding sound, 'ear' as in 'hear' — start short and glide gently towards 'uh', like leaning in to listen.
slides.formation_cue: Write 'e', then 'a', then 'r', close together — three letters, one sound.
slides.action: Cup a hand behind your ear and lean your head in gently, saying ear-ear.
slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="ear" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="ear"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.heading: Thu
slides.objective: Extra practice blending and segmenting everything taught this week — no new content today.

slides.dictation: A coin is in a jar.

slides.heading: Fri
slides.objective: Revisit everything taught this week, read the matched decodable book, and check how securely it has been learned.
